title: Relay contract v9: fold in ork's 2026-10-23..26 relay run and retrospective

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork (`../ork`) ran 40+ slices as slice relays under contract v8 from 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-26, wrote a retrospective (`ork/docs/review-2026-10-25-relay-retrospective.md`) and built the lessons into its engine (ork adj 162-170, slices S114-S121). The contract text still describes the pre-retrospective flow, so ork's engine and a hand-run relay now follow different rules. The owner asked on 2026-10-26 to unify them through one contract version, as soon as possible.

This item bumps `RELAY_CONTRACT` to 9 once the items it depends on land, so consumers move once, not once per change. s387 (pin) lands with it, so v9 is the first version a project pins. ork then adds 9 to its accepted set (`ork/internal/roles/roles.go`, `boundary.contract`).

Owner decision needed: one v9 bundle (recommended) or a version per change.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
After the dependencies land: bump `RELAY_CONTRACT` to 9, update the contract golden fixture (s378), the CHANGELOG, and the docs that name the version. File an ork item to accept v9.

Owner decisions, 2026-10-26: one v9 bundle. The dependency slices change the contract text under v8; this item alone bumps `RELAY_CONTRACT` to 9.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`; `slicer check`; the first line of `slicer ai relay` is `Contract: relay v9`.
